title: Blended English Language Learning as a Tool for Enhancing Academic Motivation and Developing Learners' Autonomy
reason: Ukrainian-language blended-learning experiment. Moodle trace (self-initiated practice-quiz iterations) and reflective-journal regularity correlated with speaking fluency and final case score (Spearman). Meets I1/I3; scales reported with Cronbach-alpha procedure.

extraction.design: quasi-experimental EG/CG plus correlational (Spearman), mixed methods
extraction.n_quote: experiment (n=120: control group n=58, experimental group n=62), questionnaires based on
extraction.population: technical-university students in professional English courses, 1 university
extraction.lms_indicators: Moodle logs: number of self-initiated attempts on practice lexico-grammar quizzes; regularity of reflective journal (Learning Logs) entries
extraction.outcome_or_construct: speaking fluency in synchronous classes; final communicative case score; also motivation/autonomy (group contrasts only)

effect_sizes.between: number of self-initiated practice-quiz iterations (Moodle) ↔ speaking fluency in synchronous classes
effect_sizes.quote: лексико-граматичних тестах і вільністю мовлення на синхронних заняттях (𝜌 = ... 0,68;𝑝 < 0,01);

effect_sizes.between: regularity of reflective-journal entries ↔ final communicative case score
effect_sizes.quote: (Learning Logs) та оцінкою за підсумковии комунікативнии кеис (𝜌 = 0,54;𝑝 < 0,01).

extraction.notes: Sample for the correlations not stated (presumably EG n = 62). How fluency was scored is not described. English abstract describes the rho = 0.54 outcome as 'overcoming the language barrier', the body as the final case score. Cronbach alpha given only as threshold (≥ 0.80). Language: Ukrainian.
